summary: Satkari Mukhopadhyaya is an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar who served as Coordinator of the Kala Kosa Division at the Indira Gandhi National Centre for the Arts (attested 1999, 2026).
Satkari Sharma Vangiya is a scholar in the fields of Indology and linguistics who studied under the traditional teachers Ramachandra Shastri Vyakaranacharya and Ramachandra Sastri (attested 1970).

Satoru Harada is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies who earned an M.A. from the University of Tokyo (attested 1973). He held posts at Toyo Bunko, the Eastern Institute, and Kokushikan University (attested 2010–2015).

Satoru Noriyama is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Esho Mikogami. He held teaching posts at Osaka University of Foreign Studies (attested 1995) and Ryukoku University (attested 2003, 2013).
Satoshi Fujiwara is a Buddhist studies scholar who served as a researcher at the Shinran Buddhist Center (attested 2015) and as a lecturer at the Otani Academic Society (attested 2026).
Satoshi Hayashima is a Buddhist studies scholar who was a research student at Ryukoku University (attested 2013–2014) and later served as a lecturer there (attested 2015–2017).

Satoshi Hiraoka studied at Bukkyo University and the University of Michigan under Shozen Kumoi, Takao Kagawa, Luis Oscar Gómez, and Gregory Schopen. He taught at Bukkyo University and Kyoto Bunkyo University, where he became professor and president.
Satoshi Ito is a scholar of Japanology, religious studies, and Buddhist studies who studied at Waseda University (~1980–1990) and served as a professor at Ibaraki University (attested 2007).
Satoshi Kono is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Sinology who earned a doctorate in literature from the University of Tokyo and became a professor at Kogakkan University in 2000.

Ryo Naiki is a scholar of history, archaeology, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and Buddhist studies who earned a PhD from Kyoto University and served there as Assistant Professor (attested 2016–2020).
Satya Narayan Goenka, active in Buddhist and religious studies, studied under Sayagyi U Ba Khin (~1955–1971) and founded the Vipassana Research Institute in 1985.

Satya Swarup Misra, an Indologist and linguist, served as Professor and Head of the Sanskrit Department at the University of Lucknow (attested 1958) and Professor of Indology and Linguistics at Banaras Hindu University (~1980–1995).

Satya Vrat Shastri studied at the University of the Punjab and Banaras Hindu University. A scholar of Indology and linguistics, he was Head of Sanskrit at Delhi University and Vice-Chancellor of Shri Jagannath Sanskrit Vishvavidyalaya.

Satyanad Kichenassamy studied at the École Normale Supérieure and Pierre and Marie Curie University. He held positions at the Courant Institute, the University of Minnesota, the University of Reims Champagne-Ardenne, and Paris Sciences et Lettres University.

Satyendra Nath Bose was educated at Hindu School, Presidency University, and the University College of Science, Technology & Agriculture. He taught at the University of Dhaka and Calcutta University, and served as Vice-Chancellor of Visva-Bharati University (~1956–1958).

Saurabh Singh studied at the University of Delhi, Guru Gobind Singh Indraprastha University, and Deccan College. He served as Principal Investigator at Bhandarkar Oriental Research Institute (2022–2023) and Adjunct Assistant Professor at Delhi University (2024).

Sayadaw U Pandita was a Buddhist studies figure who studied under Nandasiri Sayadaw and Mahasi Sayadaw. He taught at Mahasi Sasana Yeiktha, succeeded Mahasi Sayadaw, and founded and served as abbot of Panditarama Meditation Center.

Sayadaw U Sīlānanda studied under U Paññāvanta, Mahasi Sayadaw, and at University College, Colombo. In Buddhist studies, he taught at Mandalay University, served as Chancellor of the International Theravāda Buddhist Missionary University, and founded Dhammānanda Vihara.

Sayadaw U Thittila studied under Ashin Adiccavamsa and at Visva-Bharati University. In Buddhist studies, he served as librarian for the Adyar Library and the Buddhist Society, and became Lecturer in Buddhist Philosophy at the University of Rangoon (1952).
Sayagyi U Ba Khin was a teacher in Buddhist and religious studies who studied under Saya Thetgyi (~1937–1945) and founded the International Meditation Centre.
